yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point survives: the bald question, the portrait, the reading list, the four books, the $1.12, the mock report, the holidays and the telegram P.S. Small shifts: "nobody's doing any study" overstates studying getting left out, and "I reckon" softens the certainty of "Oh, see, I know!".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "verandah roof" for porch roof, "cranky old thing" for snappy, "a bit odd" for queer, "chockers" for cluttered, "pocket money" for allowance, "beaut time". "mates" for a girl's friends is fine.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural throughout: "I've got four on the go at once", "I haven't let on to anybody", "what she's on about", "If you can't be bothered writing". "down to a tee" is spelt oddly but heard naturally.
yarn-dinkum.register: A light-to-moderate Aussie layer, close to level 2, with no swearing: "Hooroo, Daddy", "See ya in January", "merry Chrissie", "cos" and "ya won't believe this" push slightly past a light touch.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Judy's eager, teasing, self-mocking voice is whole: "(that _would_ mark me as a bit odd)", and the mock-formal geometry report is kept intact.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads as if written so: "I look forward to the evening all day, and then I hang an "engaged" on the door"; no pile-ups.
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "heaps", "chockers", "beaut", "let on", "on the go", "Hooroo", "Chrissie", none repeated.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the letter: the interruptions by bells, the deadpan "Sir" report and the telegram joke all survive.

yarn-deadset.meaning: Nearly word for word, so every point survives: "I have it planned exactly what you look like--very satisfactorily".
yarn-deadset.sense: The few swaps fit: "verandah roof", "cranky old thing", "dressing gown", "pocket money", "first-year".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Swaps are real Australian, but some sit oddly in the untouched formal prose: "a properly assorted family and a home and mates and a library know by absorption" and "I find that I am the only girl at uni"; "Good-by" sits beside "merry Chrissie".
yarn-deadset.register: Largely untranslated: only spelling and a few single-word swaps ("heaps of others", "uni", "Chrissie"); lighter than level 2.
yarn-deadset.tone: The original's tone is intact because the text is: "Oh, you see, I know! You're a cranky old thing with a temper."
yarn-deadset.flow: Reads smoothly except where a slang word lands in a stiff sentence: "girls with a properly assorted family and a home and mates".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the original, since it barely changes it.

unharnessed.meaning: Every point survives; "left by the wayside" and "staying back" carry the original. The emphasis shifts from _am_ to "I'm _properly_ stuck", harmless.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly exact: "crabby old thing", "chock-a-block", "hop into my nice red dressing-gown". "the study's getting left by the wayside" strains: 'the study' reads as a room.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural: "I haven't told anybody, mind", "what she's on about", "I've got four on the go at once". Some lines stay stiff: "a proper assortment of family".
unharnessed.register: A light, even Aussie layer at about level 2, no swearing: "Hooroo, Daddy", "chock-a-block", "on the go".
unharnessed.tone: The playful voice and the deadpan report are kept: "We're finding the road rough going and very uphill."
unharnessed.flow: Mostly smooth, with a clunk: "a sort of sprinkly grey sort of hair" and "I've got it all worked out exactly what you look like".
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "chock-a-block", "hop into", "mind", "on about", "Hooroo"; nothing leaned on.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the letter retold, bells, report and telegram intact.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Facts survive, but it adds a lot of commentary: "Don't think I didn't notice.", "the man was a serial bridegroom", "(Like a bush track after rain, Sir, and about as much fun.)", "Fair's fair." Mostly colour hanging off the original, though it changes the letter's density.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly fits, but "This letter gets interrupted more than a footy commentator." misfires: commentators do the interrupting; and "set in concrete" is fine.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Much is natural ("I've got four on the go", "Haven't let on to a soul"), but some lines are bolted-on bush colour in an American college girl's letter: "the kind you could shelter a cattle dog under", "Like a bush track after rain", "meself".
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 2: a constant run of tags and similes, "ay", "aren't ya?", "poor bloke", "ripper time", "whack an"; no swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: Judy's whimsy is there but over-egged, and the asides break the deadpan of the mock-formal report: "(Like a bush track after rain, Sir, and about as much fun.)"
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively and readable; the fragments sometimes stack up: "Stumped. Is it white hair? Black hair?" and "Bliss."
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisable, but the restraint that made the letter itself (a girl's naive candour, the straight-faced report) is buried under added jokes.

engine.meaning: Essentially the original; every point survives.
engine.sense: The few swaps fit ("verandah roof", "heaps of others", "Chrissie"), but "a beautiful time in holiday" is not a sense at all.
engine.authenticity: What little is Aussie is natural, but it keeps US forms ("bath robe", "allowance", "Freshman") and makes an un-English phrase: "I’m going to have a beautiful time in holiday".
engine.register: Barely translated: spelling plus "heaps", "verandah", "Chrissie". Far lighter than level 2.
engine.tone: The original's tone survives untouched: "You’re a snappy old thing with a temper."
engine.flow: Reads like the original except for the broken "in holiday".

yarn-dinkum.quote: You're a cranky old thing with a temper, I reckon.
yarn-dinkum.original: Oh, you see, I know! You're a snappy old thing with a temper.
yarn-dinkum.why: The tag hedges a line whose joke is Judy's mock certainty.
Usually spelt 'to a T'; and it shifts 'very satisfactorily' (pleased with her picture) to 'exactly'.

yarn-dinkum.quote: everyone's so excited that nobody's doing any study
yarn-dinkum.original: everybody is so bubbling over with excitement that studying is getting left out
yarn-dinkum.why: Overstates: studying is neglected, not abandoned, and 'bubbling over' is lost.

yarn-deadset.quote: a properly assorted family and a home and mates and a library know by absorption
yarn-deadset.original: a properly assorted family and a home and friends and a library know by absorption
yarn-deadset.why: 'mates' dropped into a formal Edwardian sentence jars.

yarn-deadset.quote: Good-by till January--and a merry Chrissie!
yarn-deadset.original: Good-by till January--and a merry Christmas!
yarn-deadset.why: Archaic 'Good-by' left beside 'Chrissie': a mixed register.

yarn-deadset.quote: I find that I am the only girl at uni
yarn-deadset.original: I find that I am the only girl in college
yarn-deadset.why: 'uni' among the original's formal phrasing reads as a word swap, not a voice.

yarn-deadset.quote: I have it planned exactly what you look like--very satisfactorily
yarn-deadset.original: I have it planned exactly what you look like--very satisfactorily
yarn-deadset.why: Most of the text is left as the original, too light for level 2.

unharnessed.quote: a sort of sprinkly grey sort of hair
the study's getting left by the wayside
unharnessed.why: 'the study' reads as a room or an object, not studying.

unharnessed.quote: I've got it all worked out exactly what you look like
unharnessed.original: I have it planned exactly what you look like
unharnessed.why: Awkward construction kept from the original's syntax after changing the verb.

unharnessed.quote: Bye till January--and a merry Christmas!
unharnessed.original: Good-by till January--and a merry Christmas!
unharnessed.why: Sign-off left plain after 'Hooroo' earlier; a missed spot, not an error.

yarn-troppo.quote: This letter gets interrupted more than a footy commentator.
yarn-troppo.original: This is a very interrupted letter.
yarn-troppo.why: The simile doesn't work: commentators interrupt, they aren't interrupted.

yarn-troppo.quote: (Like a bush track after rain, Sir, and about as much fun.)
yarn-troppo.why: Added aside breaks the joke of the deadpan, formal 'Sir' report.

yarn-troppo.quote: the kind you could shelter a cattle dog under
yarn-troppo.why: Stock bush colour bolted on to a simile that was already complete.

yarn-troppo.quote: I'm only just finding out how far down it goes meself
yarn-troppo.original: I am just realizing the depths myself

yarn-troppo.why: Added line; plus many similar asides make the text heavier than a level-2 brief.

engine.quote: I’m going to have a beautiful time in holiday
engine.original: I’m going to have a beautiful time in vacation
engine.why: Broken English: a mechanical swap of vacation for holiday.

engine.quote: I have it planned exactly what you look like--very satisfactorily
engine.original: I have it planned exactly what you look like--very satisfactorily
engine.why: Left essentially untranslated; far under a level-2 brief.

engine.quote: Good-by till January--and a merry Chrissie!
engine.original: Good-by till January--and a merry Christmas!

summaries.yarn-dinkum: The best balance: a natural, light Aussie layer that keeps every point and Judy's voice; a couple of small shifts.
summaries.yarn-deadset: Faithful but barely Aussie: spelling and a handful of word swaps, some of which jar in the untouched prose.
summaries.unharnessed: A well-judged light Aussie retelling, faithful and natural, with a couple of clunky phrases.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and varied but over-embellished for a level-2 brief, with some stage-bush colour and a misfiring simile.
summaries.engine: The original with spelling changes and three word swaps, one of which breaks the grammar.
